title: Phase-2 independently re-checkable research claim record
description: The minimal shared claim-record and source-lineage schema. canonical_mechanism is the normalized atomic proposition, not a display title. snapshot_sha256 binds the exact evidence snapshot actually consulted; source_lineage retains the route back to origin and derived witnesses.

evidence_tier.description: E1 verbatim primary evidence; E2 mechanically independent multi-source agreement; E3 one source or one rail; E4 degraded-fetch inference rather than extraction.

snapshot_sha256.description: sha256 of the exact bytes at locator when this lineage entry was written.

named_consumers.phase-1-dedup: Builds stable identities and semantic/source-aware duplicate keys.
named_consumers.phase-4-contract-authoring: Turns claims into evidence-bounded, freshness-gated, executable contract clauses.
named_consumers.phase-12-refutation: Reopens exact evidence bytes, walks support/contradiction edges, and runs falsifiers.

field_justification.necessity: Stable dedup identity, contract reference, and graph node key.
Normalized atomic proposition used for semantic dedup and contract text.
Distinguishes same-looking claims from different evidence and reopens the evidence route.
Caps the strength of contract language to E1-E4 evidence quality.
Selects risk language and escalation thresholds without inventing precision.
Supplies executable acceptance criteria and a named falsifier.
Makes explicit support and contradiction graph traversal possible; an empty array records examined absence.
Blocks stale claims from silently gating contracts and exposes version-skew refutations.
Binds the contract and refutation to the exact evidence bytes actually consulted.

discarded_unconsumed_fields.reason: No named consumer needs display text distinct from canonical_mechanism.
No named consumer uses author identity; provenance is source lineage.
No named consumer can depend on an untyped notes bag.

fixture.honesty_note: Windows 05-ECO primary bytes are not mounted on this Linux worktree. Each claim's primary locator is a local excerpt under probes/RES-0001/fixtures/excerpts/ whose snapshot_sha256 is the live digest. Historical Windows locators remain as derived hops.

settling_probe.falsifies_when: Either client accepts and executes the unknown field, or both reject it the same way.

settling_probe.falsifies_when: A no-bump commit is visible to the installer as a new version.
